Issues.Title: fix(forms): guard NgForm deferred registration against a missing container
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [ ] Build related changes

- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes

## What is the current behavior?

`NgForm.addControl` and `NgForm.addFormGroup` register into the parent container in a deferred microtask without a null check, while `removeControl` and `removeFormGroup` are null-safe. When a nested control or group is destroyed in the same tick its add-microtask was queued, `_findContainer` returns `null` and `registerControl` throws `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'registerControl')`.

Issue Number: #69440

## What is the new behavior?

`addControl` and `addFormGroup` skip registration when the container no longer exists, matching the remove path. `_findContainer` now returns `FormGroup | null` so the type reflects what it can return. Two regression specs in `directives_spec.ts` cover a control and a nested group being added after their parent group was removed.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

This is the minimal version of the fix proposed in the issue. The older #69543 touches more files and adds a new error code; it has had no activity since July.

I confirmed the crash and the fix against the published `@angular/forms` 22.2.3 using `NgForm` directly. I could not run the Bazel test suite locally, so the new specs are relying on CI.

Issues.Title: refactor(docs-infra): use the router's platform Navigation API integration
Issues.Body:
adev had a hand-rolled adapter (`initializeNavigationAdapter`) that intercepted a Navigation API `navigate` event on every Router navigation and resolved/rejected it around the view transition and navigation end, so the browser could show a loading indicator on the tab and visitors could cancel a navigation with the stop button or the escape key.

The Router now provides this natively with
`withExperimentalPlatformNavigation()`, which drives the Router through the Navigation API, aborts the Router navigation when the navigate event is aborted (stop button, escape key, superseding navigation) and handles traversals and rollbacks of cancelled navigations. Use it instead and remove the adapter, along with the `transitionCreated` subject that only existed to feed it.

The feature is only enabled when `window.navigation` is available: `PlatformNavigation` is backed by `window.navigation` and has no server implementation, so enabling it unconditionally would break SSR and prerendering, as well as browsers without Navigation API support. Those fall back to the regular history-based `Location`, as before.

Since in-memory scrolling is enabled, the Router intercepts navigations with `scroll: 'manual'`, so scrolling is still handled by `AppScroller`.

Old PR: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/71023
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(docs-infra): use the router's platform Navigation API integration" (#71504)

Issues.Title: refactor(router): make setupAndRunResources consistently asynchronous
Issues.Body:
Previously, `setupAndRunResources` could return synchronously (via `return;` resulting in `undefined` to `switchTap`) when `newlyCreatedRoutes` or `targetRouterState` was missing or when `abortSignal.aborted` was true, whereas normal navigations returned a Promise and ran asynchronously.

This change marks the `switchTap` callback in `setupAndRunResources` as `async` and awaits `Promise.all(resourceSetupPromises)` and `Promise.all(blockingResourcePromises)`. This ensures `switchTap` consistently receives a `Promise` across all transition states, preventing accidental mixed synchronous/asynchronous execution within the route resources feature.

Issues.Title: fix(forms): annotate field context helpers with this: void
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Destructuring `valueOf`, `stateOf` or `fieldTreeOf` from a field context, the same pattern the JSDoc examples use, triggers `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method` (and oxlint's `typescript/unbound-method`, which mirrors it):

```ts
hidden(p.company, {
  when: ({stateOf, valueOf}) => valueOf(p.type) !== 'a' || stateOf(p.type).hidden(),
});
```

```
Avoid referencing unbound methods which may cause unintentional scoping of `this`.
```

The rule fires because these members are declared with method syntax on `RootFieldContext`. At runtime they are already safe to destructure: `FieldNodeContext` binds `stateOf` and `fieldTreeOf` in its constructor, and `valueOf` is an arrow-function field.

Issue Number: N/A (related: #65547, where `unbound-method` was mentioned in passing)

## What is the new behavior?

`valueOf`, both `stateOf` overloads, and `fieldTreeOf` declare `this: void`, so the public types match the existing runtime contract and destructuring no longer triggers the lint rule. Type-only change, no runtime behavior change. The API golden is updated.

A new spec in `field_context.spec.ts` destructures each helper in `disabled`/`hidden`/`readonly` rules and asserts the resulting field state, so dropping one of the `.bind(this)` calls would fail CI. I confirmed the spec fails with the binds removed.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

`this: void` adds no runtime parameter, and `ctx.valueOf(...)`-style calls still type-check.

## Other information

A similar library-side fix was made in kysely-org/kysely#1553 for the same lint rule.

I (Jay) used AI for this, but have reviewed it myself (both the diff and the PR)

Issues.Title: fix(core): catch view effect errors in targeted change detection mode
Issues.Body:
When a ViewEffectNode becomes dirty without any template consumer or RefreshView flag being dirtied on its owning LView, change detection traverses the view in ChangeDetectionMode.Targeted via the HasChildViewsToRefresh branch of detectChangesInView(). Because runEffectsInView() in that branch ran outside of refreshView()'s try/catch, errors thrown by view effects on subsequent targeted updates bypassed ancestor ON_ERROR handlers (such as @boundary and programmatic onError).

Extract handleViewError() and wrap runEffectsInView() in the HasChildViewsToRefresh branch so view effect errors are routed through ancestor ON_ERROR boundaries. Also clear the active reactive consumer while invoking onError callbacks so effects created inside an onError handler do not throw NG0602.

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): use canonical exported symbol in NgModule ɵmod types and skip .d.ts extra imports
Issues.Body:
### Problem
1. When an `NgModule` imported/exported a `const` alias of another `NgModule` (`export const AliasedModule = ActualModule`), `ɵmod` emitted `[typeof ActualModule]` using the unimported local name instead of the module-qualified reference `[typeof i1.ActualModule]`.
2. When `emitDeclarationOnly` and `generateExtraImportsInLocalMode` were both enabled, `ngp` emitted bare `import './child';` side-effect imports in `.d.ts`-only mode, which `ngtsc` suppresses because side-effect imports in `.d.ts` files widen the typecheck program graph.

### Solution
1. Add `refToTypeExpression` in `compiler-utils.ts` and use it for `R3NgModuleMetadataGlobal` declarations/imports/exports so `ɵmod` type arguments emit `i1.ActualModule`.
2. Guard `localCompilationExtraImports` emission in `processor.ts` with `!options.emitDeclarationOnly`.

### `ngtsc` Parity
Matches `ngtsc`'s `NgModuleDecoratorHandler` `.d.ts` type emission and `TraitCompiler` `emitDeclarationOnly` guard.

| Input | Before (`ngp`) | Now (`ngp`) | `ngtsc` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `import {AliasedModule} from './alias'` (`export const AliasedModule = ActualModule`) | `ɵmod: i0.ɵɵNgModuleDeclaration<AppModule, never, [typeof ActualModule], [typeof ActualModule]>` | `ɵmod: i0.ɵɵNgModuleDeclaration<AppModule, never, [typeof i1.ActualModule], [typeof i1.ActualModule]>` | `ɵmod: i0.ɵɵNgModuleDeclaration<AppModule, never, [typeof i1.ActualModule], [typeof i1.ActualModule]>` |
| `emitDeclarationOnly: true` + `generateExtraImportsInLocalMode: true` | Emits `import './child';` | Omits `import './child';` | Omits `import './child';` |
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler-cli): use canonical exported symbol in NgModule ɵmod types and skip .d.ts extra imports" (#71485)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): retain NgModule imports that transitively export providers via helper functions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
In `ng_module.rs`, `imports_may_export_providers` only checked `class_info.raw_imports` (which records direct identifier references). If an `NgModule` imported a standalone `@Component` (`MiddleComp`) that imported an `NgModule` (`MiddleModule`) whose providers came from a `ModuleWithProviders` helper function call (`imports: [provideFeature()]`), `imports_may_export_providers` returned `false` and `MiddleComp` was elided from `ɵinj.imports`.

### Solution
When `raw_imports` does not resolve to a provider-exporting declaration in `imports_may_export_providers`, complete the class's AST `imports` expression with `angular_foreign_resolvers()`, returning `true` if it resolves to a `ModuleWithProviders` or any reference that `may_export_providers`.

### `ngtsc` Parity
Matches `ngtsc`'s `NgModuleDecoratorHandler` transitive provider detection.

| Input | Before (`ngp`) | Now (`ngp`) | `ngtsc` |

### Problem
1. `dedup_keep_last_by` in `query/scope.rs` evicted the earlier slot and pushed the duplicate at the end (`[DirB, DirX]`), whereas JavaScript's `Map.prototype.set` in `ngtsc`'s `LocalModuleScopeRegistry` updates the value in-place at its first-seen insertion slot (`[DirX, DirB]`).
2. When an `NgModule` exported a file-local directive that was only exported from its defining module via an aliased export (`export {InternalDir as PublicDir}`), `processor.ts` emitted `i1.InternalDir` instead of the exported symbol `i1.PublicDir`.

### Solution
1. Update `dedup_keep_last_by` in `query/scope.rs` to overwrite the first-seen index in place while keeping the first-seen slot order.
2. Prefer `decl.ref.typecheckImport.symbol` over `decl.name` when rewriting cross-file `NgModule` scope declarations in `processor.ts`.

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): align constructor rest params, @Inject metadata, and ambient export = types
Issues.Body:
### Problem
1. Declarations inside `declare namespace X { ... } export = X;` were not indexed in `SyntaxFile`'s value/type-only symbol sets, so interface members (`myLib.IService`) used as constructor parameter types were treated as runtime values instead of type-only.
2. Constructor rest parameters (`constructor(...args: unknown[])`) were ignored (`target_method.value.params.rest`), emitting a valid zero-arg factory instead of `i0.ɵɵinvalidFactory()`.
3. Parameters decorated with `@Inject(TOKEN)` unconditionally forced `is_type_only = true` (`#533`), erasing runtime class types (`type: DepService` -> `type: undefined`) in `ɵsetClassMetadata`.

### Solution
1. Index value and type-only declarations inside ambient `TSModuleDeclaration` namespaces for `export =` resolution in `query/engine.rs`.
2. Extract `target_method.value.params.rest` in `get_constructor_params` and require `param.typeName != null` for `tokenResolved` in `buildDeps`.
3. Remove the `#533` `if canonical_name == Some("Inject") { is_type_only = true; }` override so `ɵsetClassMetadata` preserves runtime parameter types on `@Inject` parameters.

### `ngtsc` Parity
Matches `ngtsc` on ambient namespace `export =` DI resolution, rest constructor parameters, and `@Inject` parameter `type:` metadata.

| Input | Before (`ngp`) | Now (`ngp`) | `ngtsc` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `constructor(svc: myLib.IService)` (`IService` in `declare namespace myLib` + `export = myLib`) | `ɵfac`: `i0.ɵɵinject(myLib.IService)` | `ɵfac`: `i0.ɵɵinvalidFactory()` | `ɵfac`: `i0.ɵɵinvalidFactory()` |
| `constructor(...args: unknown[])` | `ɵfac`: `new (t \|\| RestService)()` | `ɵfac`: `i0.ɵɵinvalidFactory()` | `ɵfac`: `i0.ɵɵinvalidFactory()` |
| `constructor(@Inject(TOKEN) dep: DepService)` | `ɵsetClassMetadata`: `type: undefined` | `ɵsetClassMetadata`: `type: DepService` | `ɵsetClassMetadata`: `type: DepService` |

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): align template cycle detection and tsconfig file ordering with ngtsc
Issues.Body:
### Problem
1. Purely type-only imports (`import type {Foo}` / `import {type Foo}`) were included as edges in the static import graph used for template cycle detection, causing false-positive `ɵɵsetComponentScope` remote scoping.
2. Template dependency cycle breaking checked each component edge against the base static import graph independently, remote-scoping both sides of a 2-way component cycle instead of inserting synthetic import edges sequentially as non-cyclic edges are accepted.
3. Explicit `tsconfig.json` `"files"` entries were sorted alphabetically instead of preserving their declared `tsconfig.json` order when interning `FileId`s, changing which component in a cycle was visited first.

### Solution
1. Track runtime value imports separately from type-only imports in `imports.rs` and only feed value imports into the static import graph.
2. Insert accepted synthetic template dependency edges into the cycle graph sequentially in `hybrid_compiler.ts` (matching `ngtsc`'s `CycleAnalyzer.recordSyntheticImport`), reverting to `ɵɵsetComponentScope` for all components in a file if any component in that file closes a cycle.
3. Preserve explicit `tsconfig.json` `"files"` order in `tsconfig_resolution.rs` and pre-intern root `FileId`s deterministically in `compiler/analyzer.rs`.

### `ngtsc` Parity
Matches `ngtsc`'s `ImportGraph`, `CycleAnalyzer`, and `ComponentDecoratorHandler` remote-scoping behavior.

| Input | Before (`ngp`) | Now (`ngp`) | `ngtsc` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CompA` <-> `CompB` template cycle (`"files": ["z_first.ts", "a_second.ts"]`) | Both `ZFirstComp` and `ASecondComp` remote-scoped via `ɵɵsetComponentScope` | `ZFirstComp` imports `ASecondComp` directly; only `ASecondComp` is remote-scoped via `ɵɵsetComponentScope` | `ZFirstComp` imports `ASecondComp` directly; only `ASecondComp` is remote-scoped via `ɵɵsetComponentScope` |
| `CompC` uses `<comp-d>`, `d.ts` has `import type {CompC} from './c'` | `CompC` remote-scoped via `ɵɵsetComponentScope` | `CompC` emits `dependencies: [i1.CompD]` (no cycle) | `CompC` emits `dependencies: [i1.CompD]` (no cycle) |

Issues.Title: @angular/cli 21.2.x and 20.3.x depend on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.31.0 which is vulnerable to CVE-2026-111767, CVE-2026-111768, CVE-2026-111769 and CVE-2026-111771
Issues.Body:
### Command

other

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` versions before `1.32.0` are affected by four advisories published on 2026-10-20, all patched in `1.32.0`:

- https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-22jm-h49p-29qw (CVE-2026-111767, CVSS 8.6): "MCP TypeScript SDK: Experimental tasks were not tied to the session that created them", affected `>= 1.24.0, < 1.32.0`
- https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453 (CVE-2026-111768, CVSS 7.5): "MCP TypeScript SDK: One HTTP request within the default size limit could exhaust server memory during validation", affected `>= 1.3.0, < 1.32.0`
- https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw (CVE-2026-111769, CVSS 6.5): "MCP TypeScript client SDK: HTTP client transports and OAuth requests followed cross-origin redirects and re-sent custom headers and request bodies", affected `< 1.32.0`
- https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rvq5-wwqv-78pq (CVE-2026-111771, CVSS 6.8): "MCP TypeScript SDK: Server bearer authentication accepted tokens issued for another service", affected `>= 1.6.0, < 1.32.0`

Both LTS branches pin a vulnerable version exactly (locked on, no update allowed):

- v21 LTS: `@angular/cli` 21.2.26 through 21.2.27 (latest) depend on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.31.0` (earlier 21.2.x pinned 1.26.0 and 1.30.0, also affected)
- v20 LTS: `@angular/cli` 20.3.39 through 20.3.40 (latest) depend on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.31.0` (earlier 20.3.x pinned 1.17.3, 1.24.0, 1.25.2, 1.26.0 and 1.30.0, also affected)

v22 (22.2.x) is not affected: it depends on `@modelcontextprotocol/server` instead, pinned to the patched `2.3.1` since 22.2.2 (22.2.0 and 22.2.1 pinned `2.0.0`, updated in #34266).

The CLI only uses `McpServer` over stdio, so these do not look reachable through `ng mcp`, but the exact pin makes `npm audit` flag every install. npm's advisory feed only has GHSA-22jm-h49p-29qw and GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw so far, so the audit output below lists those two.

The fix would be bumping `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` to `1.32.1` (latest, same code as `1.32.0`) on both branches, as was done for #34263 (#34264 / #34265).

Issues.Title: @angular/build 22.2.x, 21.2.x and 20.3.x depend on vite@8.3.0 / vite@7.3.6 which are vulnerable to CVE-2026-112943
Issues.Body:
### Command

serve

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv (CVE-2026-112943, CVSS v4 6.3): "launch-editor: escapeCmdArgs() omits % escaping on Windows". vite bundles `launch-editor` into its dist, so the fix only ships with a vite bump.

Affected ranges relevant here: `vite >= 8.3.0, <= 8.3.2` (patched in `8.3.3`) and `vite >= 7.0.0, <= 7.3.6` (patched in `7.3.7`).

`@angular/build` pins a vulnerable version exactly on the active and both LTS branches:

- v22: `@angular/build` 22.2.0 through 22.2.3 (latest) depend on `vite@8.3.0`
- v21 LTS: `@angular/build` 21.2.18 through 21.2.27 (latest) depend on `vite@7.3.6` (earlier 21.2.x pinned 7.3.1 to 7.3.5, also affected)
- v20 LTS: `@angular/build` 20.3.31 through 20.3.40 (latest) depend on `vite@7.3.6` (earlier 20.3.x pinned 7.1.2 to 7.3.5, also affected)

`ng serve` keeps vite's `/__open-in-editor` middleware, so the dev server on Windows is affected. `main` is already fixed (`vite@8.3.4` in 22.3.0-next.2).

Issues.Body:
### Command

generate

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

19.x (before the v20 file naming change)

### Description

`ng generate app-shell` and `ng generate module <name> --route <path> --module <parent>` generate a component and then
reference it with a hard-coded file path and class name. Both assume the v20+ defaults (no type in the file or class
name). When the workspace configures a component `type`, the component inherits it and the hard-coded references no
longer match, so the build fails.

Workspaces get a component `type` in two common ways:

1. Every workspace updated to v20 with `ng update`: the migration that keeps the previous style guide behaviour
   (fdc6291dda) adds `"@schematics/angular:component": { "type": "component" }`.
2. `ng new --file-name-style-guide=2016`, which adds `{ "type": "component", "addTypeToClassName": false }`.

Hard-coded references:

- `packages/schematics/angular/app-shell/index.ts`: `withAppShell(AppShell)` and
  `insertImport(..., 'AppShell', './app-shell/app-shell')`.
- `packages/schematics/angular/module/files/.../__name@dasherize__-routing__typeSeparator__module.ts.template` (and the
  non-routing module template for `--route` without a routing module): `import { <%= classify(name) %> } from './<%= dasherize(name) %>';`

The library schematic had the same problem (#26981) and was fixed in 661609e3e by passing an explicit `type: ''` to the
component schematic.

### Minimal Reproduction

**app-shell** (updated-workspace configuration):

```sh
ng new ws --defaults
cd ws
# what `ng update` to v20 adds to angular.json under projects.ws.schematics:
#   "@schematics/angular:component": { "type": "component" }
ng generate app-shell
ng build
```

Generated `src/app/app-shell/app-shell.component.ts` contains `export class AppShellComponent {}`, but
`src/app/app.config.server.ts` contains:

```ts
import { AppShell } from './app-shell/app-shell';
...
provideServerRendering(withRoutes(serverRoutes), withAppShell(AppShell))
```

**module --route** (2016 file name style):

```sh
ng new ws --no-standalone --file-name-style-guide=2016 --defaults
cd ws
ng generate module feature --route feature --module app
ng build
```

Generated `src/app/feature/feature-routing.module.ts`:

```ts
import { Feature } from './feature'; // the file is feature.component.ts
```

```text

✘ [ERROR] TS2307: Cannot find module './app-shell/app-shell' or its corresponding type declarations. [plugin angular-compiler]
✘ [ERROR] Could not resolve "./app-shell/app-shell"

# module --route
✘ [ERROR] Could not resolve "./feature"
✘ [ERROR] TS2307: Cannot find module './feature' or its corresponding type declarations. [plugin angular-compiler]
```

Node.js           : 24.15.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.12.1
Operating System  : darwin arm64
@schematics/angular : 22.2.3

  extension/type"). Same code on `21.2.x` and `22.2.x`.
- Suggested fix: follow 661609e3e and pass `type: ''` (and `addTypeToClassName: false`, so the class name stays

Issues.Title: `ng generate component/directive --module` declares a class that doesn't exist when `addTypeToClassName` is `false`
Issues.Body:
### Command

generate

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

The `addTypeToClassName` option was added in 21.0.0, and the declaration code was not updated, so it never worked.

### Description

When a component or directive is generated into an NgModule with `addTypeToClassName: false` and a `type` set, the
generated class and the symbol added to the NgModule don't match:

- The component/directive class is named without the type (e.g. `Widget`), as configured.
- The NgModule `declarations` (and `exports` with `--export`) import the name **with** the type
  (e.g. `WidgetComponent`), so the build fails.

This is the configuration that `ng new --no-standalone --file-name-style-guide=2016` writes to `angular.json`:

```json
"@schematics/angular:component": { "type": "component", "addTypeToClassName": false },
"@schematics/angular:directive": { "type": "directive", "addTypeToClassName": false }
```

The component and directive schematics compute the class name with `addTypeToClassName`
(`packages/schematics/angular/component/index.ts`, `packages/schematics/angular/directive/index.ts`), but the shared
`addDeclarationToNgModule` helper always appends the type:

```ts
// packages/schematics/angular/utility/add-declaration-to-ng-module.ts
const classifiedName =
  strings.classify(options.name) + (options.type ? strings.classify(options.type) : '');
```


### Minimal Reproduction

```sh
ng new ws --no-standalone --file-name-style-guide=2016 --defaults
cd ws
ng generate component widget --module app
ng build
```


Generated `src/app/widget/widget.component.ts`:

```ts
export class Widget {}
```

Updated `src/app/app.module.ts`:

```ts
import { WidgetComponent } from './widget/widget.component';

@NgModule({
  declarations: [App, WidgetComponent],
```

The same happens for `ng generate directive ... --module`.


### Exception or Error

```text
✘ [ERROR] TS2305: Module '"./widget/widget.component"' has no exported member 'WidgetComponent'. [plugin angular-compiler]
✘ [ERROR] NG1010: Value at position 1 in the NgModule.declarations of AppModule is not a reference
```

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.3
Node.js           : 24.15.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.12.1
Operating System  : darwin arm64
@schematics/angular : 22.2.3
```

- Introduced together with `addTypeToClassName` in e417c89f9e (#31053, v21.0.0). The same code is on `21.2.x` and `22.2.x`.
- Suggested fix: let `addDeclarationToNgModule` use the class name computed by the calling schematic (or honour
  `addTypeToClassName`), so the declaration matches the generated class. Happy to send a PR with specs for the

Issues.Title: unit-test builder (Vitest): key `fsModuleCache` on the served build output instead of forcing it off
Issues.Body:
### Command

test

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Since f0a74e8f0 (released in 22.2.3), `@angular/build:unit-test` forces `fsModuleCache: false`, at the root and on the test project, overriding the `runnerConfig`. The reason is sound: Vitest keys its file system module cache on the file found on disk, while a test entry point is served from its bundle, which also holds the application code the spec imports. Changing an imported file without touching the spec left the key unchanged, and the cache served a stale bundle.

Vitest provides a hook for exactly this case: a plugin can add its own part to the cache key with `defineCacheKeyGenerator`, from `configureVitest`. The `angular:test-in-memory-provider` plugin already implements `configureVitest` and holds `buildResultFiles`, the files its `load()` serves, each with a content hash. Keying the cache on the served build output (the output file hash plus its source map hash) removes the staleness at its root, so the cache does not need to be turned off.

Since #34337 (also in 22.2.3) the test bundles are byte-identical from one build to the next, so such a key is stable and the cache can be reused across runs and CI pipelines.

Measured on a workspace application with 255 spec files (warm Angular cache, macOS, runs alternated on an idle machine), the builder patched as described:

| builder | Vitest duration | `ng test` wall time |
|---|---|---|
| 22.2.3 (cache forced off) | 21.4 s, 21.4 s | 36.6 s, 37.9 s |
| patched, warm `fsModuleCache` | 20.0 s, 18.4 s | 35.8 s, 35.8 s |

The gain is modest here, since execution dominates this suite; it grows with the share of transform time. On the same workspace, changing a file imported by a spec (without touching the spec) makes that spec fail as expected, and reverting the change reuses the original cache entry.

I have a fix ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

### Minimal Reproduction

1. In a project using `@angular/build:unit-test` with Vitest 5, set `fsModuleCache: true` and `fsModuleCachePath: './.vitest-cache'` in the `runnerConfig`.
2. Run `ng test --no-watch`.
3. No `.vitest-cache` directory is created: the builder overrides the option.

_No response_

### Summary
- Forward `warnings` from `compilationInstance.initialize(...)` into the formatted warnings output.
- Run syntactic and option diagnostics (`DiagnosticModes.All & ~DiagnosticModes.Semantic`) when `useTypeChecking` is `false`.
- Run `diagnoseFiles` even when `stylesheetErrors.length > 0` so `AotCompilation` drains `affectedFiles` into `diagnosticCache` (preventing dropped template diagnostics on subsequent watch rebuilds), and ensure `diagnosePromise` cannot cause an unhandled rejection.
- Pass `'css'` as the language for inline `<style>` tags in external `.html` templates when calling `stylesheetBundler.bundleInline(...)`.
- Only clear previous file references for a target file right before `buildState.addFileReferences(...)` when stylesheet bundling succeeds on incremental builds, preserving existing transitive references if bundling fails.
- Do not add `.d.ts` files to `changedDtsFiles` when only `.d.ts.map` changed while `.d.ts` content remained identical, avoiding redundant `bundleAllDts` passes in watch mode.

Issues.Title: perf(@angular/build): wire module resolution and package.json caches in Angular host
Issues.Body:
### Summary
- **Always wire `host.resolveModuleNameLiterals` with `resolutionCache` and `packageJsonCache`**: Previously, module resolution was only wired on `host` inside `if (hostOptions.fileReplacements)`. When `fileReplacements` was `undefined` (as in `@angular/build:library` and most application builds), `NgCompilerHost.wrap` fell back to its own internal `ts.createModuleResolutionCache` without `packageJsonCache`, leaving `host.getModuleResolutionCache()` empty and `packageJsonCache` unused across watch rebuilds and `.d.ts` module specifier generation. Using `resolveModuleNameLiterals` also replaces the deprecated `resolveModuleNames` hook and passes `containingSourceFile.impliedNodeFormat`.
- **Break `previousProgram` retention chain in `ensureSourceFileVersions`**: Compute any missing `ts.SourceFile.version` fields upfront during `ensureSourceFileVersions` instead of wrapping `program.getSourceFiles` in a closure that retains `previousProgram` across watch rebuilds.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): improve library bundler resolution and watch shared chunk consistency
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes module resolution issues in `createMemoryFileLoaderPlugin` and ensures shared chunk consistency during partial watch-mode rebuilds in the `@angular/build:library` bundler pipeline:

- **Trailing slash normalization**: Strip trailing slashes from relative directory specifiers (`import './dir/'`) before probing candidate extensions so `.../dir/index.js` is resolved instead of `.../dir//index.js`.
- **`.mjs` -> `.d.mts` declaration preference**: In `.d.ts` bundling mode, prefer `.d.mts` when an explicit `.mjs` specifier is used and both `.d.ts` and `.d.mts` exist.
- **Windows drive-letter paths**: Recognize normalized POSIX paths with Windows drive letters (`C:/...`) as internal modules in `resolveId` rather than marking them as external.
- **Watch-mode shared chunk consistency**: When a partial watch rebuild includes entry points that previously emitted shared chunks (`fesm2022/shared-*.mjs` or `types/shared-*.d.ts`), expand the Rolldown invocation to include all entry points present in the in-memory `esmFiles` / `dtsFiles` maps and update `bundleResults` for all bundled entry points so shared chunk hashes and stale file cleanup remain consistent.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/build): improve library bundler resolution and watch shared chunk consistency" (#34440)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): invalidate inline stylesheet load cache when component file changes
Issues.Body:
## Summary

When an inline stylesheet's containing `.ts` file is modified, `ComponentStylesheetBundler.invalidate()` previously deleted `entry` from `#inlineContexts` and disposed its `BundlerContext` without invalidating `#loadCache`.

- Always invalidate `#loadCache` for `angular:styles/component:${entry}` when deleting `entry` from `#inlineContexts` as well as for all `normalizedFiles`.
- Allow `MemoryLoadResultCache.invalidate()` to directly evict cache keys in `#loadResults`.
- This ensures inline SCSS `@use` errors recover when a missing partial is created, inline template Tailwind utility changes invalidate cached inline styles, and obsolete `angular:styles/component:${entry}` keys are evicted.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/build): invalidate inline stylesheet load cache when component file changes" (#34438)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): report TypeScript declaration emit diagnostics

Issues.Title: perf(@angular/build): avoid TS AST eviction and d.ts re-emit on external resource edits
Issues.Body:
This PR implements two watch-mode incremental build optimizations for external Angular component resources (`templateUrl` and `styleUrl`):

1. **Register external stylesheet dependencies on `stylesheetFile ?? containingFile`**:
   Previously, `transformStylesheet` in the library builder registered `result.referencedFiles` directly against `containingFile` (the component `.ts` file). Editing an external stylesheet or an imported SCSS partial therefore added the component `.ts` file to `effectiveModifiedFiles`, evicting the `.ts` file from `TypeScriptCompilation`'s AST cache and forcing TypeScript to re-read and re-parse the `.ts` file on disk. By registering external stylesheet references on `stylesheetFile ?? containingFile`, `expandModifiedFiles` expands an edited `_partial.scss` to `comp.scss`, which `getResourceDependencies` then maps to `comp.ts` via `resourceModifiedFiles` without evicting the cached `ts.SourceFile` AST.

2. **Skip `.d.ts` re-emit (`EmitOnly.Js`) for unchanged `ts.SourceFile`s on resource-only edits**:
   Persists a `WeakSet<ts.SourceFile>` (`emittedDtsSourceFiles`) on `AngularCompilationState` across incremental watch builds. When a component's `ts.SourceFile` object is unchanged in memory (i.e. only its external `.html` template or `.scss`/`.css` stylesheet was modified), the fallback emit loop passes `EmitOnly.Js` to `program.emit()`, skipping redundant `.d.ts` generation and downstream declaration bundling/processing.

Issues.Title: fix(material/datepicker): clear invalid text when the form value is reset
Issues.Body:
Fixes #33978.

## Problem

`writeValue` skipped re-formatting the input when the incoming value was the same as the current one. This was added in #32447 and #32485 to work around signal forms writing the same value back into the CVA while the user was typing (#32442, #32475).

As a side effect, an unparseable value could no longer be cleared programmatically. After the user types something like `foo`, the model value is `null`, so `reset()` / `setValue(null)` calls `writeValue(null)` with the value that's already there and gets skipped. The invalid text stays in the input, and because `_lastValueValid` is reset, no `matDatepickerParse` error is shown either. Signal forms `reset()` goes through the same path and is affected as well.

## Fix

Angular 22.0.0 deduplicates `writeValue` calls in the CVA interop (angular/angular@2e9aeea0f), and `@angular/material` 22 requires `@angular/core ^22.0.0`, so the workaround is no longer needed. This PR removes it so `writeValue` always re-formats the input, and drops the now-unused `reformat` parameter from `_assignValueProgrammatically`.

## Tests

- Replaced the two reactive forms specs that simulated the old signal forms loopback (and asserted the text is kept) with a spec that `reset()` clears invalid text.
- Added signal forms specs using the real `[formField]` integration:
  - invalid text is not cleared while typing (#32475)
  - a valid date is not re-formatted while typing (#32442)
  - `reset()` clears invalid text

I also checked it manually in an Angular / Material 22.2.3 app, before and after patching:

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Reactive forms: type `foo`, then `reset()` | `foo` stays | cleared |
| Reactive forms: type `bar`, then `setValue(null)` | `bar` stays | cleared |
| Signal forms: type `foo`, then `reset()` | `foo` stays | cleared |
| Signal forms: type `foo` | kept | kept |
| Signal forms: type `1` → `1/` → … → `1/1/2026` | not clobbered | not clobbered |
| Signal forms with `debounce`: same typing sequences | not clobbered | not clobbered |
| Programmatic valid date (reactive and signal) | formatted | formatted |
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(material/datepicker): clear invalid text when the form value is reset" (#33979)

Issues.Title: bug(aria/combobox): ComboboxPopup throws NG0950 when destroyed before its first change detection
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description `ComboboxPopup.ngOnDestroy` calls `this.combobox()._unregisterPopup()`. The `combobox` input is `input.required()`. If the view that holds the popup is destroyed before its first update pass, the input was never set, and reading it throws `NG0950: Input "combobox" is required but no value is available yet`. Angular reports this as "Error during cleanup of component", and in tests it fails the test ("1 fixture threw errors during cleanup"). This happens in any unit test that creates a component containing a combobox and does not run change detection before teardown, for example a plain "should create" test, or a test that only checks providers. ### Reproduction ```ts import { Component } from '@angular/core'; import { TestBed } from '@angular/core/testing'; import { Combobox, ComboboxPopup, ComboboxWidget } from '@angular/aria/combobox'; import { Listbox, Option } from '@angular/aria/listbox'; @Component({ imports: [Combobox, ComboboxPopup, ComboboxWidget, Listbox, Option], template: `
Pick one
alpha
 `, }) class Repro {} it('destroys cleanly before the first change detection', () => { const fixture = TestBed.createComponent(Repro); expect(() => fixture.destroy()).not.toThrow(); // throws NG0950 }); ``` ### Expected Behavior Destroying the popup without a first change detection does nothing (there is nothing to unregister). ### Actual Behavior `NG0950: Input "combobox" is required but no value is available yet`, from `ComboboxPopup.ngOnDestroy` (`src/aria/combobox/combobox-popup.ts`, line 67 on `main`). A possible fix: register in `ngOnInit` and keep the registered combobox in a field, then unregister that field (if set) in `ngOnDestroy`, instead of reading the input again. Issues.Title: bug(aria/menu): any DOM change inside an open submenu moves focus up and collapses it
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description Any DOM change inside an open `ngMenu` (a ripple, an icon that renders late, an `@if` inside an item) moves focus back up the menu tree and collapses the open submenu, even though no menu item was added, removed or moved. What happens: 1. `Menu` starts `_collection.startObserving(this.element)` in `afterNextRender`. The `MutationObserver` in `SortedCollection` bumps `_version` on any `childList` change in the menu's subtree. 2. `orderedItems` has no `equal`, so every bump produces a new array, and `Menu._items` / `_itemPatterns` change identity too. 3. The `afterRenderEffect` in `Menu`'s constructor that calls `this._pattern.listBehavior.goto(activeItem)` tracks the item list by accident: `ListFocus.focus()` reads `inputs.items()` through `isListDisabled()`. So it re-runs and focuses the menu's active item. 4. Focus moves from the open submenu to an item in a menu above it, and `MenuPattern.onFocusOut` closes the submenu. Possible fixes (any one of these avoids it): - Give `SortedCollection.orderedItems` an element-wise `equal`, so a version bump that changes no order isn't propagated. - Read the item list `untracked` in the `goto(activeItem)` effect; it only needs to re-run when `visible()` changes. - Bump `_version` only when an added node contains a registered item (the `TODO(ok7sai)` in `SortedCollection` already plans to replace the observer). ### Reproduction StackBlitz link: not attached. The standalone component below is the whole reproduction; it needs only `@angular/aria` (bootstrapped with `provideZonelessChangeDetection()`). ```ts import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core'; import { Menu, MenuItem, MenuTrigger } from '@angular/aria/menu'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [Menu, MenuItem, MenuTrigger], styles: `[data-visible='false'] { opacity: 0.3; }`, template: `
Item A
Item B
Item B1
Item B2
Last item @if (menuB2.visible() && tick() % 2) { • }
`, }) export class App { protected readonly tick = signal(0); constructor() { setInterval(() => this.tick.update((n) => n + 1), 1000); } } ``` Steps to reproduce: 1. Focus **Open** and press Enter. 2. Press ArrowDown, ArrowRight, ArrowDown, ArrowRight. Focus is now on **Last item**, with both submenus open. 3. Wait up to a second, until the `@if` renders its dot. ### Expected Behavior The submenus stay open and focus stays on **Last item**: the change adds no menu item, so the menu state shouldn't change. ### Actual Behavior **Item B2** collapses (`aria-expanded="false"`) and focus moves to **Item B2**. Without the `@if` (or with the interval removed), both submenus stay open and focus stays on **Last item**. It reproduces every time, and the same way with a third submenu level. ### Environment - Angular: 22.1.4 - CDK/Material: @angular/cdk 22.1.4; @angular/aria 22.1.4 and 22.2.3 (the code involved is unchanged in 22.3.0-next.2) - Browser(s): Chromium 153 - Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS

Issues.Title: fix(aria/combobox): relay every key pressed back to back to the popup
Issues.Body:
Fixes #33973.

`ComboboxPattern` relays keys to the popup through a signal that holds only the latest event, and an effect re-dispatches it later. When two keys arrived before the effect ran, the first was overwritten and never reached the popup, so quick Down, Down, Down moved once and fast typeahead lost characters.

The key handlers now queue each event, and the effect dispatches every queued event to the popup in order. I added a spec that sends keys back to back and checks that each one is handled; it fails without the change.

Issues.Title: bug(material/menu): menu restores focus to its trigger after a menu item opens a dialog (animations disabled / prefers-reduced-motion)
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

 When a mat-menu item opens a MatDialog and animations are disabled (provideNoopAnimations / animations disabled, or the user's OS has reduced motion so `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` matches), the dialog ends up with no focus: focus is moved back to the menu trigger behind the dialog's backdrop.

Cause: with animations disabled the dialog's initial focus runs synchronously during the menu item's click (in the microtask after the click listener). The click then reaches the menu panel, which emits `closed('click')`, and `MatMenuTriggerBase._destroyMenu` calls `this.focus(this._openedBy)` unconditionally, without checking where focus currently is. With animations enabled the dialog focuses ~150ms later, after the menu has closed, so the problem doesn't show.

Since `prefers-reduced-motion` comes from an OS setting (e.g. Windows "Animation effects" off), regular users hit this, and keyboard and screen-reader users land on a control hidden behind the modal.

This was reported in #14879, which was closed as a duplicate of #11696 before the reporter clarified it only happens with NoopAnimationsModule; it was then locked. The menu code on `main` still restores focus unconditionally.

Possible fix, following the dialog's own guard from #17300 ("don't move focus if it was moved during close animation"): in `_destroyMenu`, when the close reason is `'click'`, skip restoring focus if it is already inside a different overlay pane (not the menu's own pane, not a menu panel such as a submenu, and not the overlay pane that contains the trigger itself). Every other close (Escape, Tab, backdrop click, programmatic close) keeps today's
behaviour. This doesn't change the accessibility position in #11696: focus still returns to the trigger whenever the menu owns it; it only stops the menu from pulling focus out of a modal that an item just opened. Happy to send a PR with tests if this direction is acceptable.

### Reproduction

  StackBlitz (from #14879, older Angular/Material):
  https://stackblitz.com/edit/checkbox-reactive-2zhjpp?file=app%2Fapp.component.ts

  I wasn't able to save a new StackBlitz, so this links the reproduction from #14879. The bug is not specific to that
  old version:

  - It reproduces on Angular 21.2.25 / @angular/cdk + @angular/material 21.1.2 in an application with animations
  disabled through the OS setting (Windows "Animation effects" off, so `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` matches and
  Material disables its animations). After a menu item opens a MatDialog, `document.activeElement` is the menu trigger
  behind the dialog's backdrop, not the dialog's `cdkFocusInitial` button.
  - The cause is unchanged on `main`: `MatMenuTriggerBase._destroyMenu` in `src/material/menu/menu-trigger-base.ts`
  still ends with

      if (this.restoreFocus && (reason === 'keydown' || !this._openedBy || !this._triggersSubmenu())) {
        this.focus(this._openedBy);
      }

    with no check of where focus currently is, so whenever the dialog takes focus before the menu finishes closing
  (always the case with animations disabled), the menu takes it back.

  Steps (old StackBlitz, which uses NoopAnimations):
  1. Open the StackBlitz and click the menu trigger.
  2. Click the menu item that opens the dialog.
  3. In the console, run `document.activeElement`: it is the menu trigger, not the dialog's button.

  Single-file reproduction for current versions (Angular/Material 21; paste as main.ts in a new Angular project):

  import {Component, inject} from '@angular/core';
  import {bootstrapApplication} from '@angular/platform-browser';
  import {MatButtonModule} from '@angular/material/button';
  import {MatMenuModule} from '@angular/material/menu';
  import {MatDialog, MatDialogModule} from '@angular/material/dialog';

  @Component({
    imports: [MatButtonModule, MatDialogModule],
    template: `
      <mat-dialog-content>Delete this item?</mat-dialog-content>
      <mat-dialog-actions>
        <button mat-button mat-dialog-close cdkFocusInitial>Cancel</button>
        <button mat-button [mat-dialog-close]="true">Delete</button>
      </mat-dialog-actions>
    `,
  })
  export class ConfirmDialog {}

  @Component({
    selector: 'app-root',
    imports: [MatButtonModule, MatMenuModule, MatDialogModule],
    template: `
      <button mat-button [matMenuTriggerFor]="menu">Menu</button>
      <mat-menu #menu="matMenu">
        <button mat-menu-item (click)="open()">Open dialog</button>
      </mat-menu>
    `,
  })
  export class App {
    private dialog = inject(MatDialog);
    open() { this.dialog.open(ConfirmDialog); }
  }

  bootstrapApplication(App);

  On 21, emulate reduced motion (DevTools > Rendering > "Emulate CSS media feature prefers-reduced-motion: reduce", then
  reload) or set the OS animation setting off, then click Menu > Open dialog and check `document.activeElement`.

### Expected Behavior

Focus stays on the dialog's initial focus target (the "Cancel" button with cdkFocusInitial), showing its focus indicator, exactly as it does when animations are enabled. The menu should not move focus back to its trigger while an overlay opened by the menu item holds focus.

### Actual Behavior

The dialog opens, but focus is on the menu trigger ("Menu") behind the dialog's backdrop: document.activeElement is the trigger button with cdk-focused / cdk-mouse-focused. The dialog shows no focused control, Enter re-activates the hidden trigger, and Tab starts from outside the dialog. The dialog's FocusTrap did focus "Cancel" first; the menu's _destroyMenu then called focus() on the trigger. 

document.activeElement after the dialog opens: button.mat-mdc-menu-trigger  (the menu trigger, behind the backdrop)

### Environment

  - Angular: 21.2.25
  - CDK/Material: 21.1.2 (the same unconditional restore is still in src/material/menu/menu-trigger-base.ts on main)
  - Browser(s): Chrome <your version>; also reproduced in an embedded Chromium. Any browser with animations disabled or
  prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
  - Operating System: Windows 11 (Settings > Accessibility > Visual effects > Animation effects: Off)

Issues.Title: fix(multiple): allow aria tab and accordion panels without content directive
Issues.Body:
The `ngTabPanel` and `ngAccordionPanel` directives warn in dev mode that they need `ngTabContent` or `ngAccordionContent` to render, but content placed directly in a panel already renders. It's created eagerly and stays in the DOM, and the panel gets the `inert` attribute while hidden.

This removes the warning, making eager rendering a supported alternative to the content directive. A single tab group or accordion can then mix eager panels with lazy ones, which keep or remove their content depending on their own `preserveContent`.

Rendering eagerly also means the content is included in server-rendered HTML, unlike lazy content.

Fixes #33950

Issues.Title: fix(material/datepicker): update parse error with signal forms when value stays null
Issues.Body:
Fixes #33740.

When a datepicker input is bound to a signal form with `[formField]`, the `matDatepickerParse` error goes stale whenever the model value stays `null`:

- typing an unparseable value (e.g. `foo`) into an empty input does not add the error;
- erasing an unparseable value does not clear it, so the form stays invalid on an empty field (the case in the issue).

## Cause

Signal forms compute the errors of a CVA's legacy validators in a `computed` that re-runs when the control value changes or when the validator calls its `registerOnValidatorChange` callback. In `MatDatepickerInputBase._onInput()`, the `null` to `null` path calls `_cvaOnChange(null)`, which signal forms ignore because the value did not change, and it never calls `_validatorOnChange()`: that call was only in the branch for a non-null, unchanged date. Reactive forms don't hit this, because `setValue` always re-runs the validators.

## Fix

Call `_validatorOnChange()` whenever the parse state flips while the value stays the same, including `null` to `null`. The branch that already did this for an unchanged non-null date behaves as before.

With reactive forms, the `null` to `null` case with a changed parse state now also triggers `updateValueAndValidity()` after the `setValue(null)` call. It gives the same result, with one extra `valueChanges`/`statusChanges` emission in that case.

## Testing

Two tests in `datepicker.spec.ts` use a real signal form (`form()` + `FormField`). Both fail on `main` and pass with this change:

- typing `foo` into an empty input sets `matDatepickerParse`;
- setting a date, typing `foo`, then clearing the input removes it.

`//src/material/datepicker:unit_tests_chromium` (407 tests, including the date range input) and `//src/material/input:unit_tests_chromium` pass locally.

Issues.Title: build: fix API docs extraction of directives and imported types
Issues.Body:
The ARIA and CDK API pages on angular.dev are missing information, because the API extraction can't resolve several imports:

- 8 aria directives are shown as classes, and their inputs and outputs as plain properties, because their host directives are imported from another package.
- The drag-drop target doesn't use the import map, so `@angular/core` doesn't resolve, and its imports of other cdk packages aren't available. Most of its directives and its NgModule are shown as classes, and their inputs and outputs as plain properties.
- Many types are shown as `any`.

The extraction doesn't report any of this, because it ignores Angular compilation errors.

## Changes

Extraction rule:
- Map an import map entry to its target's own entry point, and fail if it doesn't exist. Currently, the rule picks the shortest `index.d.ts` among the target and its dependencies, which maps `@angular/aria/private` to `src/cdk/platform/index.d.ts`.
- Resolve relative imports of files outside `srcs` to the type declarations among the inputs, by setting `rootDirs` to include the bin directory. This mirrors how `ts_project` sees sources and declarations. A new `deps` attribute provides declarations that the import map doesn't.
- Map wildcards of directory entries relative to the directory itself, so that subpath imports like `rxjs/operators` resolve.
- Treat missing compiled stylesheets as empty, since they aren't inputs of the action and don't affect the docs.
- Fail on Angular compilation errors.

Targets: all of them use the wrapper with the import map, and those with relative imports of other packages (aria, drag-drop and three cdk/testing targets) get `deps`.

## Effect on the generated docs

Compared with `main`, 46 of the 110 aria and cdk API pages change:
- 13 classes are shown as directives and one as an NgModule, and their inputs and outputs as such, e.g. `readonly id = input<string>()` instead of `readonly id: InputSignal<any>`, or `@Input('cdkDragData') data: T` instead of `data: T`.
- Types shown as `any` show their real type, e.g. `Signal<boolean>` instead of `Signal<any>`, or `Subject<{ source: DragRef<any>; event: MouseEvent | TouchEvent; }>` instead of `any` for `DragRef.started`.
- Members inherited from base classes that now resolve are listed.
- The `Combobox` page no longer links `DeferredContentAware` to `/api/aria/private/DeferredContentAware`, which doesn't exist.

No page or member is removed, and no type gets worse. The remaining `any`s are declared as such in the source.

## Testing

- Every docs target builds on `main` and on each commit. Comparing all fields of the generated JSON, each commit only changes what its message describes.
- Each fix is needed: removing it brings its errors or `any`s back. Moving the remaining cdk/testing targets to the wrapper and removing the unused import map entry don't change the output, and neither does the stricter entry point for the remaining import map entries, which already resolve to their own entry point.
- `bazel build //...`, `pnpm lint` and the aria/combobox unit tests pass.

Issues.Title: bug(aria/tabs): the tab list loses its only Tab stop when the active tab is removed after an interaction
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

When the tab that currently holds the roving `tabindex="0"` (the *active* tab, `TabListPattern.activeTab`) is removed from the tab list after the user has already interacted with the list, **no remaining tab gets `tabindex="0"`**. Every tab ends up with `tabindex="-1"`, so the tab list is no longer reachable with `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` (WCAG 2.1.1 / 2.4.3).

It is easy to hit with `selectionMode="explicit"`, where the active tab (focus) and the selected tab can differ, but the cause does not look specific to it: any removal of the active item after the first interaction should behave the same.

Cause, from reading the source (the guard is still on `main`): `TabListPattern.setDefaultState()` is the only place that re-assigns `activeItem`, and it is guarded.

```js
setDefaultStateEffect() {
  if (this.hasBeenInteracted()) return;   // never runs again after the first interaction
  this.setDefaultState();
}
// onKeydown / onClick / onFocusIn: this.hasBeenInteracted.set(true)
```

After the first focus / key / click, `hasBeenInteracted` stays `true`. If the active tab is then destroyed, `activeItem` still points to the removed tab, so no tab in `items()` matches and the roving `tabindex` is `-1` everywhere. Nothing falls back to the selected tab or to the first focusable tab.

A possible fix is to re-run the default-state logic when the active item is no longer part of `items()`, regardless of `hasBeenInteracted`:

```js
setDefaultStateEffect() {
  const active = this.activeTab();
  if (this.hasBeenInteracted() && active !== undefined && this.inputs.items().includes(active)) return;
  this.setDefaultState();
}
```

Related: #33934 (same area of code, but about a focus moved by a script, not about a removed active tab); #32969 / 0f5b0eee introduced the `hasBeenInteracted` guard.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/duypg9mo?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.ts

Steps to reproduce:
1. `Tab` into the tab list (focus lands on `A`), press `ArrowDown` once: focus moves to `B`, which is now the active tab (`tabindex="0"`); `A` stays selected because the selection is explicit.
2. Press `Tab` three times: the panel itself, the input, then the `remove B` button.
3. Press `Enter` on `remove B`: the active tab `B` is destroyed.
4. Inspect the tabs: `A` and `C` both have `tabindex="-1"`.
5. Press `Shift+Tab` repeatedly: focus goes back through the input and the panel, then to the previous focusable element of the page. The tab list is skipped entirely.

Reproduced on `@angular/aria` 22.2.1 and 22.2.3.

### Expected Behavior

After the active tab is removed, a remaining tab (the selected one, else the first focusable) becomes the active tab and gets `tabindex="0"`, so the tab list keeps exactly one Tab stop.

### Actual Behavior

All tabs have `tabindex="-1"`. The tab list cannot be reached with `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`, and the arrow keys cannot help since focus cannot enter the list.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.1
- CDK/Material: `@angular/aria` 22.2.1 and 22.2.3, `@angular/cdk` 22.2.1 and 22.2.3
- Browser(s): Microsoft Edge (Chromium), also driven with real key events over the Chrome DevTools Protocol
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): Windows 11

Issues.Title: bug(mat-datepicker): date parse errors are not propagated to Signal Forms
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

The datepicker input provides a matDatepickerParse validation error when the user enters text that cannot be parsed as a date.

This error is available when using Reactive Forms, but when using Signal Forms, the error does not reach the errors signal of the field tree. The value of the form field stays as `null`.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-d3y2q7gw?file=src%2Fmain.ts,src%2Fmain.ts

Steps to reproduce:
1. Start the application.
2. Enter an invalid date string into the Reactive Forms datepicker.
3. Observe that the control reports a matDatepickerParse error.
4. Enter the same invalid date string into the Signal Forms datepicker.
5. Observe that the Signal Forms field does not report the corresponding parse error in field().errors().

### Expected Behavior

I would expect the date parse errors to also be available to the Signal Form.

If I understand correctly, this seems to be in line with the direction of the Angular Signal Forms API, for example with https://angular.dev/api/forms/signals/transformedValue to report parse errors in custom controls.

### Actual Behavior

The date parse errors are not available to the Signal Form. Since the form value remains as `null` for invalid values, distinguishing between an empty form and invalid input is not possible in the schema.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.2
- CDK/Material: 22.2.2
- Browser(s): Chrome, Firefox, Safari
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS

Issues.Title: bug(COMPONENT): Angular ARIA tab must allow eager loading of tab content
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

## Description

Angular Aria's tabs implementation appears to require tab panel content to be declared using `ng-template[ngTabContent]`, which prevents consumers from eagerly rendering tab panel content in the DOM.

This is problematic for use cases where all tab panels need to be initialized upfront, rather than lazily instantiated when their associated tabs become active. For example, a tab panel may contain a component that needs to initialize early, or preload data that is required for SEO (in SSR setup).

Currently, `ngTabContent` can only be applied to an `ng-template`, and the implementation warns when a tab panel does not contain the expected content directive. Applying `ngTabContent` directly to a component or a regular element does not work because it does not match the directive's selector.

It would be useful to provide a supported way to eagerly instantiate tab panel content while retaining the existing tab panel API and accessibility behavior.

## Reasoning

The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide recommends automatic tab activation on focus when the associated panel can be displayed without noticeable latency. It also notes that this typically requires panel content to be preloaded; otherwise, automatic activation introduces delays that significantly hinder efficient keyboard navigation.

Eager loading is therefore a legitimate use case for accessible tabs, particularly when panel content requires initialization or data fetching before it can be displayed.

Providing an explicit mechanism for eager content instantiation would allow developers to avoid unnecessary delays during tab navigation without having to implement their own tab behavior or work around the current content directive requirements.

### Reproduction

Link: https://angular.dev/guide/aria/tabs#example-1



### Expected Behavior

I expect the ngTabContent to have a selector on its own without the ng-template infront, so that the tab content can be eagerly loaded

### Actual Behavior

The ngTabContent selector has ng-template in front of it which prevents us from eagerly loading tab content that may contain useful information and is needed upfront and without layout shift

### Environment

- Angular: latest
- CDK/Material: N/A
- Browser(s): latest
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): N/A
